properties.details_shown: Fog, tar, and gulls; the far piers are rotting. Morning fog still sits on the docks; the party meets Sela at the end of pier four.

sources.quote: Morning in Gullwick. The fog is still sitting on the docks, gulls everywhere, and you're standing at the end of pier four looking for a boat.

changes.why: Adds the pier where the party meets its boat contact.

properties.role: Tide-reader and boatwoman at Gullwick Docks; grey braid and salt-stained coat.
properties.played_as: Whispers as if the water might hear; avoids eye contact, watches the tide line, and returns to mending her net.
properties.knows: Says Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang, forty years ago; her grandmother said the rising water was warm.

sources.quote: There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net. Grey braid, salt-stained coat. She doesn't look up.
Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.
She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye. She keeps her gaze on the tide line.
Sela, Sella, the dockhands say it both ways.
Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Introduces the named boatwoman and preserves her manner and attributed account.

sources.quote: Morning in Gullwick. The fog is still sitting on the docks, gulls everywhere, and you're standing at the end of pier four looking for a boat.
There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net. Grey braid, salt-stained coat. She doesn't look up.

changes.why: Records where the party met Sela.

change.name: Sela's account of the Saltmere flood

properties.statement: Sela says Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang, forty years ago; she reports her grandmother's account that the water came up warm.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Adds an attributed historical connection between the mine and the bell.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Identifies the mine in Sela's account.

properties.next_step: Sela offers a daylight row to the old chapel and says she will be at pier four tomorrow at first light.

sources.quote: Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.
She shrugs and goes back to her net. She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

changes.why: Adds an offered route to investigate the bell.

properties.details_shown: Up the cliff path, closed for forty years. Entrance is a black mouth in chalk, with a half-rotted timber frame and an overturned rusted cart. Warm air smells of old candle wax. Thirty paces in, the tunnel is flooded with warm black water; wet hymn-book pages float and cling to the walls.
properties.state: Closed; tunnel flooded thirty paces inside.

sources.quote: The Saltmere Mine entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted. A rusted cart lies on its side. The air coming out of it is warm and smells like a church, like old candle wax.
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.

changes.why: Records the mine's observed condition and descriptions.

change.name: The hymn page marked M. Brand

properties.statement: A hymn-book page recovered from Saltmere's flooded tunnel describes the sea giving back what it takes and bears "M. Brand" in pencil in its margin.

sources.quote: About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.
A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".

changes.why: Records the observed clue without attributing its handwriting.

sources.quote: About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.
A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".

changes.why: Locates the recovered clue at Saltmere.

properties.role: Teo Brand's sister, named by Teo while examining the hymn page.

sources.quote: That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

changes.why: Records the named sister; her identity as Teo's sister is character background, while the handwriting and visit remain his inference.

properties.what_changed: A hymn page in Saltmere bears "M. Brand". Teo identifies the handwriting as his sister Mira's and concludes she was here; the GM has not confirmed that attribution.

sources.quote: A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".
That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

changes.why: The clue advances Teo's search while keeping his attribution distinct from the inscription.

change.name: Is Maren involved with the cult or choir?

properties.what_is_open: Vessa suspects Maren is in a cult and Oren suspects she runs the choir; these are unconfirmed player theories.

sources.quote: Okay, I bet the harbor-master is behind all this. Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.
Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.
You can think that. Roll investigation if you want to search the rest.

changes.why: Records the players' suspicion without changing Maren's established state.

sources.quote: Okay, I bet the harbor-master is behind all this. Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.

changes.why: Identifies the subject of the theory, solely as a thread relationship.

properties.details_shown: Previously described as having sunk into the bay with its bell. At low water, the roof sticks out of the bay, with the bell tower, two broken arches, and seaweed hanging from the stones. At midnight, pale shapes stand in rows on the submerged chapel floor like a congregation, then vanish when the bell stops.

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches. Seaweed hangs from the stones.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: Adds the chapel's visible architecture and the witnessed shapes.

properties.statement: Fishermen say the Kelp Mother drags children standing close to the water down by their ankles; her existence is unconfirmed.

sources.quote: Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say. They pull their boat up and leave.

changes.why: Preserves the local warning as a rumor, without creating a creature NPC.

sources.quote: (to himself) That's the choir clock at three of six.

changes.why: Advances the existing hidden story clock from two to three of six.

properties.what_is_open: Who or what rings the submerged bell? It rang twelve times again at midnight, with louder humming; pale shapes stood in rows on the chapel floor and vanished when the ringing stopped.

sources.quote: And then, right at midnight, the bell rings again under the water. Twelve times. And the humming is back, but louder. Much louder than two nights ago. You can feel it in your teeth.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: Advances the bell mystery with witnessed events, without identifying their cause.

properties.details_shown: Tavern by the docks, with a fire going and the smell of tar and fish stew.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.

changes.why: Records the named tavern where the party ends the session.

properties.role: Innkeeper at the Tarred Gull; huge, with a red beard.
properties.played_as: Laughs at his own jokes and wipes the same mug while talking; calls the party brave or stupid and gives them stew on the house.
properties.knows: Says he has known Maren for thirty years, calls her sharp-tongued with a good heart, and says she lost a brother to the bay.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.
You lot went to the shore at midnight? Brave or stupid. On the house, either way.
Bram is huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, and he wipes the same mug the whole time he talks to you.
Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Introduces the voiced innkeeper and his attributed knowledge of Maren.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.
The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

changes.why: Records Bram's workplace.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.
The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

changes.why: Records where the party encountered Bram.

change.name: Bram's account of Maren's lost brother

properties.statement: Bram says Maren lost a brother to the bay; he says he has known her for thirty years and describes her as sharp-tongued with a good heart.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Records Bram's account without certifying its truth or inventing a motive.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Identifies whom Bram's account concerns.

properties.what_is_open: Vessa suspects Maren is in a cult and Oren suspects she runs the choir. Bram describes her as sharp-tongued with a good heart and says she lost a brother to the bay. The players' allegations remain unconfirmed.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Adds Bram's differing account to the unresolved suspicion.

properties.next_step: The party plans for Sela to row them out tomorrow at first light and to dive to the chapel at low tide during daylight.

sources.quote: At low tide, during the day. Not at night, Sela was right about that.
So tomorrow, first light, Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide. I'll buy rope and a second lantern tonight.
Agreed. Tomorrow we dive.

changes.why: Records the agreed next action as a plan, not an accomplished dive.

properties.what_changed: The Saltmere hymn page bears "M. Brand". Teo identifies it as Mira's handwriting and infers the hymns came from the chapel. He agrees to a daylight chapel dive tomorrow with Sela; the handwriting attribution and hymn provenance remain unconfirmed.

sources.quote: Okay, plan. Mira wrote in that hymn book. The chapel is where the hymns came from. We go down to the chapel.
So tomorrow, first light, Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide. I'll buy rope and a second lantern tonight.
Agreed. Tomorrow we dive.

changes.why: Connects Teo's clue to his stated search plan without confirming his deductions.
